items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: And then Mario Cuomo got up and he started his speech by saying how great it was to come off the street where everything is hectic and just have some music to start with.

ctx.x: Yeah. It was. Over the years I’ve always thought being a musician, any musician that you talk with this way on camera or just hit them in a bar, if they could start telling stories you’ll have trouble getting out of the room. They’d go on forever. Any musician can do that. I’ve always thought that — first of all I’m lucky, very fortunate to be an active performing musician other than the fact that it’s something that I love and people actually pay me money to do it, which never ceases to amaze me, and the phone…

they get to travel and you never work in the same place twice — well sometimes you do — but you work in so many different places. It’s not like you’re going to your office everyday. It’s always different. So you get into a lot of unique situations and there are a lot of unique opportunities. And you never know what’s going to happen when the phone rings. It could take you anywhere, to some country you’ve never been to before, to playing a style of music that you’ve never played before. Just all kinds of…
